newsitem.title: USA: U.S. cash soymeal - Volatile CBOT scares end-users.
newsitem.headline: U.S. cash soymeal - Volatile CBOT scares end-users.

text.p: Volatile price swings in CBOT soybean prices have most soymeal end-users stepping back and waiting for the market to settle down Monday, dealers said.
"Everybody is just sitting back and trying to digest the report," said one Minnesota-based dealer.
Cash soymeal trade was quiet and most basis levels were unchanged as a result, dealers reported.

CBOT soymeal futures swung higher and lower in response to uncertainty over higher-than-expected plantings estimates from the U.S. Department of Agriculure. USDA forecast 1997 soybean acreage at 68.8 million acres, up seven percent from last year.
One dealer in Indiana reported heavy selling interest before the report came out. However, he said the interest dried up after the market opened.
"A lot of people wanted to sell it before the open, but then the report scared them off," the dealer said.
